sample_unit: patients invited to a telemonitoring program

links.outcome: Patient characteristics associated with refusing an AI virtual assistant telemonitoring program
links.effect: 59.8% accepted and 40.2% refused. Refusal was significantly associated with lower sociocultural level, fewer electronic devices, higher anxiety and depression scores, and lower inhaled therapy adherence.
links.quote: Refusal was significantly associated with lower sociocultural level, fewer electronic devices, higher anxiety and depression scores (HADS-A, HADS-D), and lower adherence to inhaled therapy (TAI).

unlisted_practices: Use participation-barrier profiles to guide patient selection strategies for AI telemonitoring

screen.reason: Evaluates factors associated with patient participation vs. refusal in a clinical telemonitoring program using an AI virtual assistant (Lola), but does not compare specific deployment practices or safeguards.
